narr: Within an unseasonably warm and moist low-level environment, a strong southwest upper level flow with an intense mid-level shortwave ejecting across the Central Plains/Midwest regions resulted in a line of strong to severe thunderstorms (along with heavy rain) across north Georgia during the evening and overnight hours of 29-30 December 2021. The remnant boundary/front settled over central Georgia during the afternoon of 30 December 2021 which resulted in redevelopment of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms. Several tornadoes, along with areas of wind damage and large hail occurred all across north and central Georgia from these events. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches occurred over the area, resulting in isolated flash flooding in the greater Atlanta metro area.
ev: The Emergency Manager reported Gregory Road closed due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that between 2 and 2.5 inches of rain occurred over the area, on top of 1.5 to 3 inches that occurred the day before. These rainfall amounts, falling on saturated soils, resulted in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Sockwell Road closed due to flooding from the Yellow River. The USGS gage (NWS MYRG1 / USGS 02207335) rose above bankfull/action stage on as a result of the rainfall, then continued to rise above Minor Flood stage to a height of 11.43 ft on December 31. Radar estimates indicate that between 2 and 2.5 inches of rain occurred over the area, on top of 1.5 to 3 inches that occurred the day before. These rainfall amounts, falling on saturated soils, resulted in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Sewell Road closed due to flooding near the confluence of the Little River and other tributaries. Radar estimates indicate that between 1 to 2 inches of rain occurred over the area, on top of 1 to 2 inches that occurred the day before. These rainfall amounts, falling on saturated soils, resulted in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Northlake Drive closed as well as flooding at the Tinsley Mill Condos off Flat Creek Road due to floodwaters from Flat Creek as it flows into Lake Peachtree. Radar estimates indicate that between 1.5 to 2 inches of rain occurred over the area, on top of 1 to 2 inches that occurred the day before. These rainfall amounts, falling on saturated soils, resulted in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding of Sleepy Hollow Road between Ralston Road and North Burnt Hickory Road due to high flow on a Gothards Creek tributary. Radar estimates indicate that between 1 to 2 inches of rain occurred over the area, on top of 2 to 4 inches that occurred the 24-hours before. These rainfall amounts, falling on saturated soils, resulted in the flash flooding.

The Public reported flooding of streets in the Carrington Lakes Subdivision due to high pool elevation of the neighborhood lakes. Radar estimates indicate that between 1 to 2 inches of rain occurred over the area, on top of 2 to 4 inches that occurred the 24-hours before. These rainfall amounts, falling on saturated soils, resulted in the rises on the area lakes.

The Public reported flooding of an apartment complex parking lot off Northlake Parkway. Radar estimates indicate that between 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain occurred over the area, on top of 2 to 4 inches that occurred the 24-hours before. These rainfall amounts, falling on saturated soils, increased runoff and resulted in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding across Winn Road near the South Paulding High School due to high flow on a Sweetwater Creek tributary. Radar estimates indicate that between 1 to 2 inches of rain occurred over the area, on top of 2 to 4 inches that occurred the 24-hours before. These rainfall amounts, falling on saturated soils, resulted in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding of the Brogdon Road and New Hope Road intersection. Radar estimates indicate that between 1.5 to 2 inches of rain occurred over the area, on top of 1 to 2 inches that occurred the day before. These rainfall amounts, falling on saturated soils, produced high runoff rates and resulted in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding of the Whitlock Complex parking lot, requiring barricades to block vehicle access. This flooding was due to high flow on White Oak Creek and other small tributaries at the confluence. Radar estimates indicate that between 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, on top of 2 to 4 inches that occurred the day before. These rainfall amounts, falling on saturated soils, resulted in the flash flooding.
